title: A Chameleon's Tongue Pulls 41 G, Far More Than a Space Shuttle
subject: veiled chameleon

scenes.text: A chameleon barely moves, yet its tongue out-accelerates a space shuttle.
Scientists measured it: about forty-one times gravity. A shuttle launch peaks around three.
The tongue is roughly two body lengths long and reaches full stretch in about seventy milliseconds.
Muscle alone can't contract that fast. So the chameleon cheats, like drawing a bow.
It stretches elastic tissue first, then lets go. The stored energy fires the tongue.
Even in the cold, the launch slows only 10 to 19 percent. Pulling it back slows far more.

description:
A chameleon's tongue accelerates at about 41 times gravity, far more than a space shuttle at launch.
It reaches full length in about 70 milliseconds, powered by stored elastic energy like a bow and arrow, so it still works when the animal is cold.
Which animal has the best secret weapon? Tell us below.
first_comment: The chameleon's tongue launch barely slows in the cold, but pulling it back slows by more than 42 percent for each 10 degrees Celsius. Which animal would you want to see in slow motion next?
